title: Silicon, Not Software, Will Decide the AI Race
gist: A teaser arguing the AI contest has moved past scientific discovery into a deployment phase where computing power, advanced semiconductors, physical infrastructure and market size — not model quality — determine who wins.

themes.theme: From Discovery Phase to Deployment Phase

insights.claim: Competition in AI has shifted from scientific discovery to deployment, so leadership now depends on computing power, advanced semiconductors, physical infrastructure, and markets large enough to justify the enormous investments required.
insights.speaker: ANTONIN BERGEAUD
insights.so_what: Reframes AI competitive advantage as capital- and infrastructure-bound, favoring incumbents with fabs, power and domestic market scale over pure model labs.
insights.quote: success increasingly depends on computing power, advanced semiconductors, physical infrastructure, and markets large enough to justify the enormous investments they require

insights.claim: Market size is itself a competitive input in AI because only large enough domestic markets can justify the scale of investment that deployment requires.
insights.speaker: ANTONIN BERGEAUD
insights.so_what: Implies structural disadvantage for mid-sized economies — including Europe — in the deployment phase regardless of research talent.

insights.claim: The transformer architecture underpinning today's large language models was introduced in 2017, the basic logic of scaling — that more computation and data produce predictably better models — was established by 2020, and ChatGPT's late-2022 launch revealed mass-market appeal and set off the global AI race.
insights.speaker: ANTONIN BERGEAUD
insights.so_what: A five-year lag between the enabling science and the commercial race suggests the current cycle is driven by deployment economics rather than fresh breakthroughs.
insights.quote: By 2020, researchers had established the basic logic of scaling: more computation and data produce predictably better models.
